target_value: ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1) ∈ M_2(K(q)) — Hoefsmit matrix in the SYT basis {T_1=[1 2 / 3], T_2=[1 3 / 2]}
description: Frontier-paydown chain: derives the Hoefsmit-matrix image of the braid generator σ_1 in the λ = (2,1) block of H_3(q), and the corresponding Frobenius character χ^{(2,1)}_q(σ_1), entirely from AXIOMs (Schur + Wedderburn + Categorical action + Hecke energy + Frobenius pairing).  No SCRIPT_CITED steps.  Together with `schur-weyl-weight-3.derivation.json`, this discharges the categorical-action and Frobenius-pairing frontier in the atom chains.

steps.name: Standard Young tableaux of shape (2,1)
steps.operation: Enumerate SYT of shape (2,1): there are exactly two, T_1 = [1 2 / 3] and T_2 = [1 3 / 2].  Each SYT corresponds to a basis vector of the Hoefsmit irrep V^{(2,1)}.
steps.notes: Mathlib has `Mathlib.Combinatorics.Young.YoungDiagram` and `Mathlib.Combinatorics.Young.SemistandardTableau`; the SYT count for λ = (2,1) is the dimension f_λ = 2 of the Hoefsmit block.

steps.name: Content function c(i) := col(i) − row(i)
steps.operation: For each SYT T and each cell containing i, define the content c_T(i) := col(i) − row(i).  T_1: c(1)=0, c(2)=1, c(3)=−1.  T_2: c(1)=0, c(2)=−1, c(3)=1.
steps.notes: Pure combinatorial extraction from the tableau coordinates; content function is the standard Schur-Weyl invariant.

steps.name: Hoefsmit recipe for ρ^λ(σ_i) on each SYT
steps.operation:
For the generator σ_i and each SYT T, apply Hoefsmit's recipe:
  - if i, i+1 lie in same row of T → σ_i acts as +q on T,
  - if i, i+1 lie in same column of T → σ_i acts as −q^{-1},
  - else (T_1 and T_2 swap by exchanging i and i+1) →
    σ_i mixes T_1 and T_2 by the matrix
      [[ −q^{-1} + q · q_int(d-1)/q_int(d) ,  √(q_int(d-1)·q_int(d+1))/q_int(d) ],
       [ √(q_int(d-1)·q_int(d+1))/q_int(d) ,  q − q^{-1} · q_int(d-1)/q_int(d) ]]
    where d := c(i+1) − c(i) is the axial distance and q_int is the q-integer.  For (2,1) and σ_1: T_1, T_2 differ by swapping 1 and 2; d = 1 − (−1) = 2.
steps.output_value: Recipe applied: σ_1 acts on V^{(2,1)} by a 2x2 matrix in the T_1, T_2 basis; explicit entries depend only on q and the contents c(1)=0, c(2)=±1.  See Kassel §III.4 Theorem 4.6.
steps.notes: Categorical action axiom: the braid generator σ_i acts on V^{⊗n} via the R-matrix; the Hoefsmit matrix is the projection of that action onto the λ-isotypic block.  Hecke energy axiom fixes the eigenvalues +q and −q^{-1} of σ_i (CLAUDE.md §7a).

steps.name: Explicit ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1) matrix
steps.operation:
Substitute d = 2 into Hoefsmit's formula.  q_int(1) = 1, q_int(2) = q + q^{-1}, q_int(3) = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}.  Compute the matrix entries.  Result:
  ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1)  =  [[ −q^{-1} + q/(q+q^{-1}) ,  √(1·(q^2+1+q^{-2}))/(q+q^{-1}) ],
                       [ √(1·(q^2+1+q^{-2}))/(q+q^{-1}) ,  q − q^{-1}/(q+q^{-1}) ]]
Each entry is a Laurent polynomial / square-root expression in q with rational coefficients (Mathlib field K(q)).
steps.output_value: ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1) ∈ M_2(K(q)) — Hoefsmit matrix in the SYT basis {T_1=[1 2 / 3], T_2=[1 3 / 2]}
steps.notes: Pure algebraic substitution; one-line application of the recipe in step 3 to the contents from step 2.

steps.name: Frobenius character χ^{(2,1)}_q(σ_1) = tr(ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1))
steps.operation:
By the Frobenius pairing, the character χ^λ_q on a Hecke element is the trace of its Hoefsmit-matrix image.  For ρ^{(2,1)}(σ_1) as above:
  χ^{(2,1)}_q(σ_1)  =  (−q^{-1} + q/(q+q^{-1}))  +  (q − q^{-1}/(q+q^{-1}))
                      =  q − q^{-1}
after telescoping.  This is the universal value of σ_i in the (2,1) block (independent of i).
steps.notes: Trace of an explicit 2x2 matrix; algebraic simplification using q_int(2) = q + q^{-1} and q_int(3) = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}.
